# select_budget (Resource)

A spend threshold over a recurring or fixed period, optionally narrowed to a team and to a slice of spend.

## About

A budget compares actual spend against `amount` for its current period, optionally narrowed to a team and to a slice of spend via `filter_expression_json`. To learn more, see the [SELECT documentation](https://select.dev/docs/getting-started).

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/budgets`. The `api_key` configured on the provider must carry the `budgets:read` and `budgets:write` scopes; without them every operation fails with an authorization error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A recurring, organization-wide budget. With no filter_expression_json, every
# dollar of spend the organization records counts toward it.
resource "select_budget" "monthly_org_wide" {
  name   = "Acme Monthly"
  amount = 50000

  period = {
    schedule_type = "monthly"
    start_date    = "2026-01-01"
  }
}

# A budget scoped to a team and narrowed to one warehouse's spend, expiring
# after four quarters.
#
# The filter's root must be a group — {"operator": "and"|"or", "filters":
# [...]} — never a bare leaf filter. A leaf at the root plans clean, because
# Terraform cannot see inside an opaque JSON string, and then 422s on apply:
# the API's structured filter only accepts a group at that position.
resource "select_budget" "analytics_team_warehouse" {
  name    = "Analytics Team - SELECT_BACKEND"
  amount  = 5000
  team_id = "2f0899e2-2746-4300-887c-524e64b5a138"

  period = {
    schedule_type             = "quarterly"
    start_date                = "2026-01-01"
    expires_after_occurrences = 4
  }

  filter_expression_json = jsonencode({
    operator = "or"
    filters = [
      {
        field    = "warehouse_name"
        operator = "in"
        values   = ["SELECT_BACKEND"]
      }
    ]
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `amount` (Number) The spend threshold for one period.
- `name` (String) The budget's display name.
- `period` (Attributes) The recurrence or date range the budget's threshold applies over. schedule_type picks the variant, and which of the other fields are valid depends on it: fixed_range needs end_date; weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly accept expires_on and expires_after_occurrences; custom needs repeat_every and repeat_unit and accepts the same two expiry fields. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--period))

### Optional

- `filter_expression_json` (String) A JSON-encoded filter narrowing which spend counts toward the budget. Null counts all spend. The root of the filter must be a group — `{"operator": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]}` — not a single leaf filter.
- `started_at` (String) When the budget takes effect. Defaults to the time it is created.
- `team_id` (String) The team to scope this budget to. Null scopes it to the whole organization. Requires permission to write budgets in that scope.

### Read-Only

- `budget_end_date` (String) When the budget itself expires. Null if it never does.
- `create_time` (String) RFC 3339 UTC creation timestamp.
- `created_by` (String) Who created the budget.
- `current_period_end` (String) The end date of the period the budget is currently in.
- `current_period_start` (String) The start date of the period the budget is currently in.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this budget. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The budget's identifier in SELECT, assigned when it is created. Use it with `terraform import` to bring an existing budget under management.
- `status` (String) The budget's current standing against its spend threshold. Measured by a daily refresh, or on demand by evaluating the budget. Null until one of those has run: creating or changing a budget does not measure it, and changing what it measures clears it again.
- `update_time` (String) RFC 3339 UTC last-update timestamp.
- `updated_by` (String) Who last changed the budget. Null if no one has since it was created.

<a id="nestedatt--period"></a>
### Nested Schema for `period`

Required:

- `schedule_type` (String) Which shape this period takes.
- `start_date` (String) The date this period's recurrence or range begins, as YYYY-MM-DD.

Optional:

- `end_date` (String) The last date of the range. Required for, and only valid with, schedule_type = fixed_range.
- `expires_after_occurrences` (Number) The number of occurrences after which the recurrence stops. Valid only for a recurring or custom schedule_type.
- `expires_on` (String) The date the recurrence stops. Valid only for a recurring or custom schedule_type.
- `repeat_every` (Number) How many repeat_units between occurrences. Required for, and only valid with, schedule_type = custom.
- `repeat_unit` (String) The unit repeat_every counts. Required for, and only valid with, schedule_type = custom.

## Import

`select_budget` can be imported using the budget's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_budget.example 2f1c8b4e-9a6d-4d1f-9d0e-7d3a5b6c8e01
```

The ID is assigned by SELECT when the budget is created, so there is nothing about your configuration that predicts it. It is the `id` attribute, and it is also the last path segment of the budget's page in the SELECT UI.

## Additional Information

### `period` is one object, not a block per schedule type

`period` is keyed by its own `schedule_type` rather than split into `fixed_range`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `yearly` and `custom` blocks: `fixed_range` requires `end_date`; the four recurring types accept `expires_on` and `expires_after_occurrences`; `custom` requires `repeat_every` and `repeat_unit` and accepts the same two expiry fields. A field that does not belong to the chosen `schedule_type` fails at plan time.

Changing `period` clears the budget's evaluated `status`, letting a monitor watching it alert again on thresholds it has already reported.

### `filter_expression_json` must be a group at its root

The value is a JSON-encoded filter, and its root must be a group — `{"operator": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]}` — never a single leaf filter. Terraform cannot see inside the string, so a leaf at the root plans clean and only fails when SELECT rejects it on apply.

Removing `filter_expression_json` from the configuration clears it, which counts all spend toward the budget rather than narrowing it.

### `team_id` clears with the same explicit-removal rule

Removing `team_id` from the configuration moves the budget to organization scope. Moving a budget between scopes requires permission to write budgets in the scope it leaves and the one it joins.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the budget's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the budget changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.

### `current_period_start`, `current_period_end` and `budget_end_date` move with the calendar

These are derived from `period` every time the budget is read, so they can change between two applies that changed nothing about the budget itself — a recurring budget's current period simply moves on.

### Deleting a budget also deletes every monitor watching it

Destroying this resource removes the budget and every monitor configured against it. Spend already recorded elsewhere is unaffected.
